indicator: College and Career Readiness indicator
who_is_counted: The four-year graduation cohort. The rate is reported one year in arrears.
how_a_student_counts: A cohort member is ready by meeting any one benchmark.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (to confirm); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Work-based learning (to confirm); Military (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: The list of benchmarks widened over the years, so the statewide rate rose with it; our page reads a school's change against that statewide rise.
our_page_measure: College and career ready (class year), the state's own rate.
sources: ALSDE School Data: Business Rules <https://www.alabamaachieves.org/reports-data/school-data/business-rules/> | Let's Measure Ready: A 50-State Analysis of College, Career, Military, and Civic Readiness Indicators (All4Ed and Urban Institute, July 2025) <https://all4ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Final_Lets_Measure_Ready.pdf>

indicator: College/Career Indicator (CCI), share of graduates Prepared
who_is_counted: Four-year graduates of the class, plus five-year graduates who were Prepared.
how_a_student_counts: A graduate is Prepared by meeting any one approved measure; many measures are combinations. The state also reports Approaching Prepared.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts in part); Work-based learning (counts on its own); Military (counts in part); Civic, service or biliteracy (counts in part); Grades, attendance or career plan (counts in part)
recent_and_coming_changes: The State Board added AP course passage in July 2025 and is reviewing new career measures (internships, student-led enterprises, simulated work-based learning, ASVAB).
our_page_measure: Prepared for college or a career (state indicator), under the rules of the 2024-25 download only (2023-24 and 2024-25).
sources: CDE, CCI Measures of College Readiness, 2025 Dashboard <https://www.cde.ca.gov/ta/aC/cm/documents/ccicollege25.pdf> | CDE, CCI Measures of Career Readiness, 2025 Dashboard <https://www.cde.ca.gov/TA/ac/cm/documents/ccicareer25.pdf> | CDE, 2025 Dashboard Technical Guide: College/Career Indicator <https://www.cde.ca.gov/ta/ac/cm/documents/dbguidecci25.docx>

indicator: Postsecondary and Workforce Readiness (PWR) indicator
who_is_counted: High schools, on five sub-indicators; worth 30% of a high school's framework points.
how_a_student_counts: Points across sub-indicators, not a single ready or not-ready status for each student.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); College credit (counts in part); Industry credential (counts in part); Military (counts in part); Graduation or college entry (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: HB25-1278 puts the SAT in the achievement indicator and rebuilds PWR around graduation, dropout, college and career readiness before graduation, and postsecondary progress. CDE expects the changes in the 2027 frameworks.
our_page_measure: School Performance Framework percent of points; the PWR indicator's own percent of points is in our build files, not yet on the page.
sources: CDE, PWR Indicator Fact Sheet <https://www.cde.state.co.us/accountability/pwr_factsheet> | Colorado General Assembly, HB25-1278 Education Accountability System <https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/HB25-1278>

indicator: College and Career Acceleration component of school grades
who_is_counted: Graduates in the graduation rate cohort; prior-year data. Worth 100 points in the school grade.
how_a_student_counts: A graduate counts by earning any one acceleration result during the four cohort years.
route_categories: AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts in part); Industry credential (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: The 2025-26 guide lists no change to this component; the high school grading scale moved up for 2025-26.
our_page_measure: College and career acceleration.
sources: FDOE, 2025-26 Guide to Calculating School Grades <https://www.fldoe.org/file/18534/SchoolGradesCalcGuide26.pdf>

indicator: CCRPI Readiness component (high school)
who_is_counted: Twelfth graders for the three readiness indicators below; the component also holds literacy and attendance.
how_a_student_counts: Each indicator is a percent of students; the indicators are weighted into one Readiness score.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Grades, attendance or career plan (counts on its own); Graduation or college entry (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: From 2025-26, completing a high-demand career pathway counts 1.5 times toward pathway completion.
our_page_measure: HOPE-eligible graduates, a related state measure, not the CCRPI readiness indicator.
sources: Georgia State Charter Schools Commission, CCRPI Overview <https://scsc.georgia.gov/document/document/ccrpi-overviewpdf/download> | GaDOE, CCRPI Readiness <https://ccrpi.gadoe.org/Reports/Views/Home/readiness.html>

indicator: Postsecondary Readiness indicator
who_is_counted: Graduates with a regular or alternative diploma and grade 12 non-graduates.
how_a_student_counts: A student is ready by meeting one type of readiness, academic or career; high-demand credentials carry more weight.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: Senate Bill 25 (2023) added the co-op and internship route and the extra weight for high-demand credentials.
our_page_measure: Postsecondary readiness, without the bonus (transition readiness in 2017-18 and 2018-19; postsecondary readiness from 2021-22).
sources: KDE, Postsecondary Readiness <https://education.ky.gov/AA/Acct/Pages/Postsecondary-Readiness.aspx>

indicator: Mississippi Readiness Index (from 2025-26); College and Career Readiness and Acceleration before that
who_is_counted: High schools and districts. Readiness is worth 150 of the 1,000 high school points from 2025-26.
how_a_student_counts: Points in three parts: acceleration, assessment and achievement.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Diploma or endorsement (counts on its own); Graduation or college entry (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: The 2025-26 Readiness Index replaces the prior college and career readiness measures, and the 2025-26 grades set a new baseline. Our page's series ends at 2024-25 under the old rules.
our_page_measure: College and career ready (2017-18 to 2024-25, old rules) and ACT composite (juniors).
sources: MDE, Understanding the Accountability System (April 2026) <https://mdek12.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/59/2026/03/2_2026-Understanding-Accountability_3.20.26.pdf> | MDE, Mississippi Public School Accountability Standards, 2025 <https://mdek12.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/5/2026/01/Mississippi-Public-School-Accountability-Standards-2025.pdf> | MDE, Readiness in the Statewide Accountability System (January 2026) <https://mdek12.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/13/2026/01/Accountability-Readiness-Webinar-1.13.26.pdf>

indicator: Success-Ready Students (MSIP 6 Annual Performance Report)
who_is_counted: Graduates, on the Annual Performance Report.
how_a_student_counts: Weighted points: assessment scores earn 0.25 to 1.25 points by score band; advanced coursework earns 1 to 1.5 points.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Graduation or college entry (counts in part)
recent_and_coming_changes: Our page's two measures follow the earlier MSIP 5 rules (classes of 2016 to 2019 and 2022).
our_page_measure: Graduates with a qualifying college or career assessment score; graduates earning advanced credit.
our_page_match: Part of the state's indicator (earlier rules)
sources: DESE, Accountability Data <https://dese.mo.gov/quality-schools/accountability-data> | Let's Measure Ready: A 50-State Analysis of College, Career, Military, and Civic Readiness Indicators (All4Ed and Urban Institute, July 2025) <https://all4ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Final_Lets_Measure_Ready.pdf>

indicator: College and Career Readiness indicator, Nevada School Performance Framework
who_is_counted: High schools; worth 25 of 100 framework points.
how_a_student_counts: Points across three measures.
route_categories: AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own); Diploma or endorsement (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: NDE is exploring tiered industry-recognized credentials for a future version of the indicator.
our_page_measure: NSPF index score; the readiness completion measure is in our build files, not yet on the page.
sources: NDE, College and Career Readiness (NSPF) <https://webapp-strapi-paas-prod-nde-001.azurewebsites.net/uploads/College_and_Career_Readiness_NSPF_05938e3c6b.PDF> | Let's Measure Ready: A 50-State Analysis of College, Career, Military, and Civic Readiness Indicators (All4Ed and Urban Institute, July 2025) <https://all4ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Final_Lets_Measure_Ready.pdf>

indicator: College, Career, and Civic Readiness (CCCR) Index
who_is_counted: The four-year cohort; a school index from 0 to 200.
how_a_student_counts: Weighted index: each student earns 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.5 or 0 by the highest credential earned.
route_categories: AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts in part); Industry credential (counts in part); Civic, service or biliteracy (counts on its own); Diploma or endorsement (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: Back in accountability from 2025-26 (based on 2024-25 results) after years as informational only. The Report Card Database carries no index for 2019-20 to 2023-24.
our_page_measure: College, career and civic readiness index (high schools): 2017-18, 2018-19, 2024-25.
sources: NYSED, CCCR Indicator Fact Sheet <https://www.nysed.gov/sites/default/files/programs/accountability/cccr-fact-sheet.pdf> | NYSED, SIRS-108 CCCR Accountability Report Guide <https://www.nysed.gov/sites/default/files/programs/information-reporting-services/sirs-108-cccr-college-career-civic-readiness-accountability-report-guide.pdf> | NYSED, Reimagine Phase amendments <https://www.nysed.gov/accountability/news/reimagine-phase-amendments-every-student-succeeds-act-essa-accountability-system>

indicator: ACT/ACT WorkKeys indicator, School Performance Grade
who_is_counted: Students meeting the benchmark on the ACT (grade 11) or ACT WorkKeys (grade 12).
how_a_student_counts: A student counts by meeting either benchmark.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: NC DPI lists the move from 19 to 17 among the 2025-26 framework updates. Math course rigor (NC Math 3) is a separate high school indicator.
our_page_measure: Share of ACT subject tests meeting ACT's subject benchmarks (not the composite of 17 the state counts); CTE concentrators earning a WorkKeys certificate.
sources: NC DPI, Accountability Framework Background Brief <https://www.dpi.nc.gov/districts-schools/accountability-and-testing/school-accountability-and-reporting/accountability-data-sets-and-reports/accountability-framework-background-brief> | NC DPI, ACT Reports <https://www.dpi.nc.gov/districts-schools/testing-and-school-accountability/school-accountability-and-reporting/act-reports>

indicator: College, Career, Workforce, and Military Readiness (CCWMR) component
who_is_counted: The four-year graduation cohort; 12.5% of the overall rating, rated from 2024-25.
how_a_student_counts: A student is ready by meeting any one of 11 measures, all weighted equally.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Diploma or endorsement (counts on its own); Grades, attendance or career plan (counts in part)
recent_and_coming_changes: Renamed and expanded from Prepared for Success; the technical assessment pathway counts from 2023-24, so our page starts the series there.
our_page_measure: College, career, workforce and military readiness (from 2023-24).
sources: Ohio DEW, Here's What Is Calculated in the CCWMR <https://education.ohio.gov/getattachment/Topics/Data/Report-Card-Resources/Traditional-Report-Cards/Here-s-What-is-Calculated-in-the-CCWMR.pdf.aspx?lang=en-US> | Ohio DEW, Guide to 2024-2025 Ohio School Report Cards <https://education.ohio.gov/getattachment/Topics/Data/Report-Card-Resources/Traditional-Report-Cards/2024-2025-Report-Card-Guide.pdf.aspx?lang=en-US>

indicator: Postsecondary Opportunities indicator
who_is_counted: Eleventh and twelfth graders; worth 10 points of the high school report card.
how_a_student_counts: A student counts by completing any one approved opportunity with a grade of D or better; it measures participation, not a score.
route_categories: Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: The 2026 report card put the statewide rate at 58% of juniors and seniors.
our_page_measure: Postsecondary opportunities indicator (0-100).
sources: OSDE, Report Card Spotlight: Postsecondary Opportunities <https://sde.ok.gov/sites/default/files/documents/files/02-04-19-Report-Card-Indicator-Spotlight-Postsecondary-Opportunities_0.pdf> | OSDE, Oklahoma Releases 2026 Public School Report Card <https://oklahoma.gov/education/divisions/media/newsroom/2026/oklahoma-releases-2026-public-school-report-card.html>

indicator: Future Ready PA Index, college and career measures
who_is_counted: Grades 5, 8 and 11 for the career standards benchmark; twelfth graders or graduates for the others.
how_a_student_counts: Separate measures, each a percent of students; no combined ready status.
route_categories: Advanced course (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own); Grades, attendance or career plan (counts on its own); Graduation or college entry (counts in part)
recent_and_coming_changes: Only the career standards benchmark is used in federal accountability; industry-based learning and rigorous courses of study are reported for information.
our_page_measure: Career standards benchmark; graduates who completed a rigorous course of study; graduates competent or advanced on an industry assessment; graduates in school, the military or work a year on.
sources: PDE, Future Ready PA Index: Review of Indicators <https://www.education.pa.gov/K-12/ESSA/FutureReady/Pages/FRReviewofIndicators.aspx> | PDE, Career Ready PA <https://www.pa.gov/agencies/education/resources/student/career-ready-pa> | Future Ready PA Index <https://futurereadypa.org/>

indicator: College and Career Readiness indicator (college ready or career ready)
who_is_counted: The graduation cohort; worth 19 points in the high school rating under the 2025-26 manual.
how_a_student_counts: A student counts as college ready or career ready by meeting any one criterion; the state also reports college AND career ready.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts in part); Industry credential (counts on its own); Career test (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Grades, attendance or career plan (counts in part)
recent_and_coming_changes: A tiered credential rule applies to students who began high school in 2024-25 (2028 report cards), and the indicator is set to change for the 2027 report cards pending federal approval.
our_page_measure: College or career ready; earning a career-ready credential; the soft skills assessment pass rate.
sources: SC EOC, 2025-26 Accountability Manual (updated June 16, 2026) <https://eoc.sc.gov/sites/eoc/files/Documents/Acct%20Manual%2025%2026/FINAL%20Accountability%20Manual%20SY%202025-26%20(UPDATED%202026%2006%2016).pdf> | Let's Measure Ready: A 50-State Analysis of College, Career, Military, and Civic Readiness Indicators (All4Ed and Urban Institute, July 2025) <https://all4ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Final_Lets_Measure_Ready.pdf>

indicator: College, Career, and Military Readiness (CCMR) component
who_is_counted: Annual graduates from the prior school year (the class of 2024 for 2025 ratings).
how_a_student_counts: A graduate counts by meeting any one indicator.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts in part); Industry credential (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Diploma or endorsement (counts in part)
recent_and_coming_changes: Credit from a sunsetting certification is capped at 5 graduates or 20% of graduates, whichever is higher.
our_page_measure: College, Career and Military Ready graduates (classes of 2017 to 2024), each class under the rule of its year.
sources: TEA, 2025 Accountability Manual, Chapter 2: Student Achievement Domain <https://tea.texas.gov/texas-schools/accountability/academic-accountability/performance-reporting/chapter-2-2025-student-achievement-domain.pdf>

indicator: Postsecondary Readiness indicator
who_is_counted: High schools; 75 of 225 points, in three 25-point parts.
how_a_student_counts: Points across three parts.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts in part); CTE completion (counts in part); Graduation or college entry (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: ACT changed its composite in spring 2026; Utah keeps the historical composite that includes science.
our_page_measure: Grade 11 students scoring 18 or higher on the ACT; mean ACT composite (grade 11).
sources: USBE, Accountability Technical Manual (August 2026) <https://schools.utah.gov/assessment/_assessment_/_resources_/_accountability_/26AccountabilityTechnicalManual.pdf>

indicator: Post-secondary Achievement indicator, Balanced Scorecard
who_is_counted: Twelfth graders.
how_a_student_counts: A student counts by meeting any one route during high school.
route_categories: AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: No change noted in our sources.
our_page_measure: Post-secondary achievement (grade 12); Leader in Me high schools appear on it in 2021-22 and 2022-23 only.
sources: W. Va. Code of State Rules 126-12-4 (Policy 2320) <https://regulations.justia.com/states/west-virginia/agency-126/title-126/series-126-012/section-126-12-4> | Let's Measure Ready: A 50-State Analysis of College, Career, Military, and Civic Readiness Indicators (All4Ed and Urban Institute, July 2025) <https://all4ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Final_Lets_Measure_Ready.pdf>

indicator: No college and career readiness indicator in accountability
who_is_counted: Not applicable.
how_a_student_counts: The report card's On-Track to Graduation priority area uses graduation, attendance, chronic absenteeism, grade 3 ELA and grade 8 math; the grade 11 ACT sits in Achievement.
recent_and_coming_changes: All4Ed's July 2025 review lists Wisconsin among the states with no readiness indicator.
our_page_measure: ACT composite, grade 11; AP exams scored 3 or above; on-track to graduation score.
sources: DPI, 2025-26 Report Card Guide <https://dpi.wi.gov/media/55842/download?inline> | Let's Measure Ready: A 50-State Analysis of College, Career, Military, and Civic Readiness Indicators (All4Ed and Urban Institute, July 2025) <https://all4ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Final_Lets_Measure_Ready.pdf>

indicator: College and Career Readiness Indicator (Distinguished Scholar; College and Career Ready Scholar)
who_is_counted: Graduating seniors; districts submit counts to ISBE.
how_a_student_counts: A student must meet every core requirement and then either earn the College and Career Pathway Endorsement or meet one academic indicator in ELA, one in math and three or more career ready indicators.
route_categories: Test score (counts on its own); AP, IB or Cambridge exam (counts on its own); Advanced course (counts on its own); College credit (counts on its own); CTE completion (counts on its own); Industry credential (counts on its own); Work-based learning (counts on its own); Military (counts on its own); Civic, service or biliteracy (counts on its own); Diploma or endorsement (counts on its own); Grades, attendance or career plan (counts on its own)
recent_and_coming_changes: ISBE's redesigned accountability framework (Profiles of Performance, October 2026) does not include the indicator, and the 2026 report card release gave participation counts rather than indicator rates.
our_page_measure: No readiness measure on our page yet.
sources: ISBE, College and Career Readiness Guidance (March 2025) <https://www.isbe.net/Documents/CCR-Guidance.pdf> | ISBE, 2026 Illinois Report Card release (October 30, 2026) <https://www.isbe.net/Lists/News/DispForm.aspx?ID=1606>
